key_insight: Adding gesture as a parallel instruction modality and embedding gesture features directly into the vision-language-action representation enables robots to resolve spatial ambiguity and select the correct object/action in cluttered scenes with similar items.
problem_solved: Existing VLA systems that rely only on textual instructions fail to disambiguate which object to act on when multiple similar objects are present; incorporating human gestures supplies explicit spatial cues to resolve this ambiguity.
method: Extract gesture signals (e.g., hand keypoints, pointing vectors, gesture masks) and encode them into a compact gesture embedding.
Fuse gesture embeddings with visual and language representations in a shared latent space via attention-based cross-modal fusion to produce gesture-aware VLA embeddings.

Condition the action decoder/policy on the fused representation and train end-to-end (or via contrastive pretraining + finetuning) on paired vision-language-gesture-action data to improve manipulation success.
impact: GesVLA makes robot instruction more natural and reliable by using gestures to disambiguate spatial references, improving real-world manipulation success and human-robot interaction without requiring verbose text instructions.
